decision.title: 7.11's open cases; one decoder, one feature data path, one array helper, one text form writer (packet )

body.p: , after , , , , , , , , , . Verified as asks: debug and debug-gcc build with -Werror, the touched unit and CLI tests pass, clang-tidy is clean on the changed files, tools/check-call-cycles.py finds no cycle (230 files), and XT40, XP40, XQ40 and XSD were run whole with the release drivers before (6e1a371) and after, case by case.

item.p: 7.11's XT40 cases: 10 of 12 pass now; the gate stays open, for these reasons:

transform-009 passes. The XT40 driver did not check assert-serialization inside assert-result-document. A serialized test case now collects its result documents serialized (the collector's SERIALIZED delivery), and assert-serialization and serialization-matches inside assert-result-document compare those bytes. Five more pass for the same reason: result-document-0201, -0212, -0285, -0286 and -0287.

transform-004 cannot pass while holds. A static variable calls fn:transform, so compiling the outer stylesheet would compile and run the inner one from inside the outer compiler's static evaluation: compiler, evaluator, fn:transform, compiler again, without bound. That is the recursion forbids. The run part already goes through the machine (EVALUATE_UNIT, ). The compile part would need a compiler that the machine can suspend, a stack of compilations, which is a design change of the XSLT compiler. Until then a static fn:transform raises FOXT0004 ().

transform-401 fails only on its pattern ~record(x, y), the "~T" type pattern of the newer draft that and left out. Checked: with the 13 October 2026 draft's equivalent, map{'x', 'y'}, the case gives <out><in>3</in></out> as expected. (owner) now targets the newest draft, and packet 4.22 brings its type patterns, so 4.22 closes this case. No pattern change is made here.

One decoder (glossary ): sxml_xml_decoder_next in src/xml_internal.h decodes UTF-8, UTF-16 in either byte order, ISO-8859-1 and US-ASCII, one codepoint a step. Its error rule is FAIL (the XML parser's transcoding; text decoding without fallback) or REPLACE (one U+FFFD per maximal subpart, Unicode 16.0, 3.9.6; Encoding Standard 8.1.1 and 14.2: text decoding with fallback and the HTML input stream). A high surrogate cut short by the end takes the rest with it, so WHATWG's single error stays single. Removed: text_decoding's own decoders and sxml_text_encoding (it is sxml_xml_encoding now); html_encoding's UTF-8 and UTF-16 decoders and its UTF-8 check (sxml_utf8_validate). One change in behaviour: fn:unparsed-text with fallback replaces a malformed sequence by one U+FFFD instead of one for each byte. Unicode recommends this, and no test case depends on it.

Full Text through the feature data path (): sxml_feature_data_request gains . The reader gains an optional read_document for the DOCUMENT_NODE form (a thesaurus). The loader's retrieval request gains asks_unresolved (an empty URI is not resolved; the resolver is also asked for a relative URI with no base, absolute_uri empty) and accepts_document_node. The public resource contract is unchanged. src/full_text_resource.c holds only the stop word and thesaurus readers now. Lost: a thesaurus delivered as bytes is parsed without the resolver's resource URI and encoding name. It needs neither.

One array helper (glossary ): sxml_allocator_reserve_array in src/memory_internal.h, beside sxml_allocator_allocate_array. It doubles from a minimum, zeroes new memory, and leaves the array unchanged on failure. Users: collation_tailoring, function_library_element_map, cldr (entries and its byte text), collation_uca, the document loader, and the XML buffer and array (xml_entity). sxml_uca_allocate_array, a copy of sxml_allocator_allocate_array, is gone.
's cheap ones:
The schema reader's xs:boolean and nonNegativeInteger read through the cast engine's lexical mapping (sxml_lexical_read_boolean, sxml_lexical_read_digits in src/cast_internal.h).

Gregorian day arithmetic: src/calendar.c adds cycle days (sxml_calendar_cycle_day_of, sxml_calendar_date_in_cycle). The day numbers are made from them. operator_temporal.c counts in them, so no int64 year overflows. cast_facet.c and the processor's clock use the calendar, and the processor's own leap-year and civil-date copies are gone.

Compile reports: sxml_schema_report_request gives subject or subject_name in place of a prebuilt detailed_description. sxml_schema_compilation_report alone writes "description: subject" (a name as Q{uri}local). The reader, resolver, assembler and content model stop building it, and the content model's 256-byte text is gone. The XPath assertion's diagnostic is now its subject.
Text forms: src/text_form.c (glossary ) is the one bounded writer under the IR, XSLT AST, schema and content-model text forms.
The three serialization heapsorts are sxml_sort_in_place. The canonical attribute order keeps the first key-lookup failure in its sort state.
Counts (release, whole suites): XT40 11,945 to 11,951 passed (130 wrong errors both times), none lost, 0 errors; XP40 32,655 and XQ40 45,914, the same case for case; XSD 41,486, unchanged.

Sizes: sxml.wasm 2,089,167 stripped, 730,367 gzipped (6.2's 2,091,192), and the guard reports +345 bytes since its baseline. sxml-full.wasm is 7,630,816 (7,637,765), and the CLI 9,223,672. All are within the budgets.
Left (not cheap here):
transform-004 (, above) and transform-401 (4.22);
XSLT's yes/no reader beside xs:boolean (another lexical space);
sxml_text_encode_codepoint's UTF-8 beside sxml_xml_buffer_append_codepoint;
cldr's byte_text, which could be an sxml_xml_buffer;
the other private growers that grep grow finds (about 30, many with their own minimums or index tables), which can move to sxml_allocator_reserve_array one at a time.
